title: Systematic review of mental health symptoms among Arab individuals in the United States
abstract: Abstract Objectives We aimed to evaluate psychosocial and demographic factors associated with depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and psychological distress among Arab individuals in the U.S. Methods In accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines, we conducted an organized search of published English literature using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and ProQuest (including APA PsycINFO). Our inclusion criteria involved observational studies (e.g., cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort) published between January 2000 and March 2024, conducted to investigate factors associated with mental health problems among Arab immigrants or refugees (adults or children) living in the U.S. Two reviewers individually extracted the article data and evaluated the reported studies’ methodological quality using a pre-established checklist. We employed a structured narrative synthesis, following Cochrane guidelines, to analyze the source study reports’ text and table data. Results We included 19 publications, representing a summed total of 8,480 study-level participants; this total may include individuals represented in more than one publication because potentially overlapping samples were identified. Across the included studies, recurrent correlates of mental health symptoms included female gender, older age, immigration-related circumstances, and perceived discrimination. Conclusion and implications In our review, we delved into mental health issues among Arab individuals in the U.S. and emphasized the significance of culturally responsive interventions/services to meet their unique needs, especially for vulnerable subgroups within the Arab community. These findings may inform consideration of culturally responsive, gender-sensitive, and age-appropriate services; however, the included studies were observational and did not evaluate intervention effectiveness. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
